Sample.evidence_source: Most papers contribute ONE study record. EXCEPTION: a paper that tests BOTH a CBT arm AND an IPT arm in the same RCT contributes TWO study records — one with IPT=0 (the CBT arm) and one with IPT=1 (the IPT arm).
Sample.warning: The paper describes two distinct CBT-flavored interventions (Self-Control Therapy and Behavioral Problem-Solving Therapy) and a Waiting List control. Following the rule that only CBT+IPT dual-arm studies create multiple records, this is treated as a single 'main sample' record with IPT=0.

IPT.evidence_source: [/page/8/Text/3] Self-Control Therapy. The self-control treatment (S-C) was modeled after the latest of Rehm's manuals for adults (Rehm et al., 1984), which combines cognitive and behavioral skills training. [/page/8/Text/5] Behavioral Problem-Solving Therapy. The behavioral problem-solving therapy (BPS) combined self-monitoring, pleasant activity scheduling, and the acquisition of problem-solving skills.
IPT.warning: Both described interventions (Self-Control Therapy and Behavioral Problem-Solving Therapy) are variants of CBT, not IPT.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/7/Text/3] Subjects were randomly assigned to experimental conditions. [/page/7/Text/4] Common Elements. Subjects in the self-control and behavioral problem-solving conditions received a behavioral rationale for the development and treatment of depression. [/page/9/Text/4] Waiting List. Following random assignment to conditions, subjects in the waiting list (WL) condition were informed that they would begin meeting with a therapist as soon as possible.
dxgive.warning: The section describes interventions and mentions 'dysphoria' and 'behavior related to depression' but does not specify formal diagnostic criteria for study entry or assessment.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/7/Text/4] Self-monitoring log sheets of pleasant activities were completed by subjects on a daily basis. [/page/8/Text/4] During the first four sessions, subjects were taught to monitor pleasant activities and positive self-statements through the use of log sheets, which consisted of lists of pleasant events and self-statements. On the bottom of each sheet, subjects rated their mood for the day on a 0-10 scale.
